newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SKATING OFFICIAL SEEKS TO LIVEN UP ICE DANCING.
newsitem.headline: SKATING OFFICIAL SEEKS TO LIVEN UP ICE DANCING.

text.p: International Skating Union President Ottavio Cinquanta on Saturday proposed a radical change for ice dance in a bid to make it less predictable and more exciting for spectators.

Cinquanta was speaking at the Bailey's Cup of Russia where, following an established trend, the ranking for all 11 couples in the ice dance remained unchanged throughout the three sections of the competition.
The ISU president told a news conference that in order to generate more spectator and media excitement in the event, ice dancers should prepare two different free dance programmes each season.
Such a change could be introduced in 1999, with the launch of the new ISU Four Continents Championships.
The ice dancers could prepare one free dance for competition in the Four Continents or European Championships and a second programme for the World Championships.
Natalia Linichuk, coach to Russian world silver medallists and Bailey's Cup winners Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov, gave a cautious welcome to the proposal.
"This is just an exchange of opinion, but I can see the progress in that. It is an interesting idea and we have to try to see if it works."
Speaking at the same news conference, Krylova added: "It would also make it more interesting if the rules were not so strict and we were allowed high lifts and different moves."
Cinquanta said a final decision was still some way off.
"This is a good discussion, but it is something for our congress to decide. Together we will find a solution."
